title: Umbreon_Rootkit_Investigation_89d
description: Investigate the Umbreon rootkit, a Pokémon-themed Linux rootkit that targets both x86 and ARM systems. It is designed to hide its presence and manipulate system processes, making it difficult to detect and remove. The rootkit uses various techniques to maintain persistence and evade detection.
outcomes: Identification of hidden files and directories

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Umbreon rootkit is a Pokémon-themed Linux rootkit that targets both x86 and ARM systems. It is designed to hide its presence and manipulate system processes, making it difficult to detect and remove. The rootkit uses various techniques to maintain persistence and evade detection.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the victim host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The victim host is connected to the victim-switch network with the IP address 192.168.50.5. The attacker host is connected to the attacker-switch network with the IP address 192.168.40.5. The passkey `start` is used to proceed to the next level of the investigation. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Identify Evidence of Shared Library Injection
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for signs of unauthorized shared library injection. Look for unusual libraries loaded into system processes that could indicate rootkit activity. The hidden flag is the name of the shared library used by the rootkit.
levels.solution: Use the `ldd` command to check the loaded libraries for system processes. Look for any suspicious or unfamiliar entries. The hidden flag is the name of the shared library used by the rootkit.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `ldd` command to check the loaded libraries for system processes and look for any suspicious or unfamiliar entries.

levels.title: Determine System-Wide Preload Configuration Modifications
levels.content: Examine the system-wide preload configuration on the victim host. Check if any unauthorized libraries are being loaded system-wide, which could indicate rootkit persistence. The hidden flag is the path to the preload configuration file.
levels.solution: Use the `cat` command to view the contents of the system-wide preload configuration file. The hidden flag is the path to the preload configuration file.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `cat` command to view the contents of the system-wide preload configuration file.

levels.title: Locate Hidden Files or Directories
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for any hidden files or directories that are not visible through standard system utilities. These could be artifacts left by the rootkit to maintain persistence or hide its activities. The hidden flag is the path to a hidden directory or file.
levels.solution: Use the `ls` command with the `-a` option to list all files and directories, including hidden ones. The hidden flag is the path to a hidden directory or file.
